U.S. Department of Justice Federal Bureau of Prisons Administration Division Field Acquisition Office Grand Prairie, Texas 75051 January 13, 2026

MEMORANDUM FOR CONTRACT FILE

FROM: Luke Bonner, Contracting Officer SUBJECT: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition – Emergency Asbestos Demolition This acquisition is for emergency asbestos demolition and debris removal services for seven staff housing structures destroyed during a tornado event at the Federal Correctional Institution in Marion, IL. The requirement includes wet demolition of remaining structural elements, removal of asbestos-containing debris, cleanup of scattered ACM-contaminated materials, mastic removal, asbestos air monitoring, and EPA-required demolition notifications. These services are necessary to restore the site to a safe condition and prevent further environmental and occupational exposure. This procurement is conducted under FAR 6.103-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency, as delay in award would result in serious injury to the Government. Environmental inspection confirmed widespread asbestos-containing materials dispersed across the site, exposed to weather, and posing an immediate health hazard. ACM debris cannot be maintained in adequately wet condition if left in place, increasing airborne fiber risk and potential regulatory noncompliance. Delays would also impede access to the area, increase environmental liability, and allow weather to further spread contaminated debris. Full and open competition would introduce delays incompatible with the urgent need to mitigate hazardous material exposure. Because the total value of this acquisition is below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold, FAR 12.102(a) applies. In accordance with FAR Part 12, the Contracting Officer has determined that only one source is available to meet the Government’s urgent need. Limited-scope market research was conducted to identify firms capable of immediate mobilization. Summit Environmental Services, Inc. was the only contractor able to provide licensed asbestos abatement personnel, mobilize immediately, perform wet demolition and ACM debris removal in compliance with EPA NESHAP requirements, conduct asbestos air monitoring, and provide required EPA notifications. Other vendors contacted were unable to meet the immediate response timeframe. Competition was therefore restricted only to the extent necessary to address the unusual and compelling urgency. The Contracting Officer will determine the price fair and reasonable through comparison to historical pricing, independent estimates, and evaluation of labor, equipment, and disposal costs typical for emergency ACM abatement. This emergency action is limited strictly to immediate hazard mitigation; future reconstruction or follow-on environmental work will be competed to the maximum extent practicable.
